observations.summary: The distributor explains how a roadway fixture distribution affected spacing and visual comfort, connecting the selected layout to project concerns.
The post explains checking site geometry, pole height, spacing and light distribution in a simulation before selecting a product change.
The designer lists AGi32 analysis, IES inputs and application types to make scope recognizable for a buyer.
The apartment project page identifies its site lighting plan and photometric site plan as distinct deliverables within a broader electrical scope.
A DIALux tutorial shows the effect of pole spacing on a parking layout. The technical comparison gives viewers a concrete visual to inspect.
observations.metrics_context: Count observed in the public search index. The platform measurement date was unavailable.

observations.summary: A team member explains how the separate tool can inspect IES or LDT distributions, metadata and comparison views before calculation, then asks where file preparation takes time.

payload.performance_read: One tool discussion has a verified November date. The historical tutorial's indexed engagement is a single observation. The examples demonstrate how designers explain options and inputs, with insufficient comparable metrics to judge which format performs best.

tests.idea: Interview electrical contractors with a two-layout mockup. Hook: “Same lot. Same criteria. What changes with the fixture?” Keep geometry, grid and criteria fixed. Show spacing, mounting height and IES assumptions. Use calculated values only after the reviewer clears the model
tests.success_metric: buyers who can state their acceptance criteria and share a real fixture cut sheet or layout request

tests.idea: Test a one-page photometrics intake card with distributors. Ask for base drawing, pole or mounting constraints, IES files and the reviewing party. Ask which required input usually arrives last
tests.success_metric: distributors who can identify an active layout and supply the missing input
